prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2395 resolves the failure in-band and per-request: it sends a JSONRPCError carrying the original request's id on read_stream_writer, so only the affected in-flight request errors out while the rest of the session keeps working; it also removes the prior `# pragma: no cover` marker (indicating new test coverage for this path) and upgrades the log line from debug to warning to match the now-handled failure. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: stdio_server's write_stream memory object stream is created with capacity 0, causing a handler trying to queue its final response to block/deadlock while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification) to the process stdout. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs edit the identical `write_stream, write_stream_reader = create_context_streams[SessionMessage](0)` line to relieve the same zero-capacity stream, but they take different approaches. #2654 changes the default to a buffer of 1 so the fix applies out of the box, and adds a dedicated regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the exact deadlock scenario of queuing a response while a progress notification write is still in flight. #2215 instead adds new `read_stream_buffer_size`/`write_stream_buffer_size` parameters defaulting to 0, so the reported blocking behavior is unchanged unless a caller explicitly opts in by passing a nonzero size — it does not fix the default-path deadlock. #2215 also has a larger API surface (two new public constructor parameters, plus read-stream buffering that is unrelated to the reported issue), while #2654's diff is a minimal, targeted default change with a comment explaining the rationale.

prs.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
prs.author: Bartok9
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the exact same branch of validate_tool_use_result_messages() to handle the case where a previous assistant tool_use is not followed by any tool_result block in the next message. The current code unconditionally computes tool_use_ids vs tool_result_ids and raises a generic 'ids do not match' error in this case. #2962 and #3053 propose opposite fixes for this same code path: #2962 skips the id-matching check entirely (via `has_tool_results and ...`) so no error is raised, citing SEP-1577 which states a tool_use is NOT required to be followed by a tool_result. #3053 keeps the original unconditional check's outer guard and instead adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` with a clearer message — i.e. it still treats a missing tool_result as an error, just with better wording. These are mutually exclusive behavioral changes to the same bug, not complementary patches. (2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously relied on naive substring/regex matching that could misfire on commas or field names embedded inside quoted parameter values (and PR #3012 explicitly removes the old `re`-based implementation). Both replace it with a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer for auth-param extraction. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously relied on naive substring/regex matching that could misfire on commas or field names embedded inside quoted parameter values (and PR #3012 explicitly removes the old `re`-based implementation). Both replace it with a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer for auth-param extraction. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3041's tokenizer (`_split_www_authenticate_segments` + `_extract_bearer_auth_params`) explicitly walks segments to find the one whose scheme token matches 'bearer' before collecting its params, so it correctly isolates the Bearer challenge when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. `Bearer ..., Basic ...`). PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only strips text before the first space and treats everything after as one challenge's params, so it does not distinguish a second scheme's params from the first challenge's params in a multi-challenge header. Both diffs are similarly sized single-file changes touching the same function, but #3041's segment-then-scheme-match design covers a case #3012's single-split design does not.

prs.title: fix(client/auth): discover AS metadata before cold-start token refresh, with issuer-binding check
prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address token refresh failing or misbehaving immediately after a process restart, because the authorization server metadata (needed to resolve the token endpoint) only ever lived in memory and is lost when the OAuth provider is reconstructed from storage. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address token refresh failing or misbehaving immediately after a process restart, because the authorization server metadata (needed to resolve the token endpoint) only ever lived in memory and is lost when the OAuth provider is reconstructed from storage. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3263 closes the gap by re-running AS metadata discovery before a cold-start refresh, adds an issuer-binding check so a rediscovered token endpoint can't be spoofed by a malicious redirect, and tracks an `eager_discovery_attempted` flag so it doesn't re-probe on every refresh — all without touching any public interfaces, so it fixes the behavior for every existing `TokenStorage` implementation immediately. #2492 instead adds new optional `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods to the `TokenStorage` protocol that default to no-ops, so the fix only takes effect once each storage backend is separately updated to implement them, leaving existing implementations unfixed out of the box.

The current code unconditionally computes tool_use_ids vs tool_result_ids and raises a generic 'ids do not match' error in this case. #2962 and #3053 propose opposite fixes for this same code path: #2962 skips the id-matching check entirely (via `has_tool_results and ...`) so no error is raised, citing SEP-1577 which states a tool_use is NOT required to be followed by a tool_result. #3053 keeps the original unconditional check's outer guard and instead adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` with a clearer message — i.e. it still treats a missing tool_result as an error, just with better wording. clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041's tokenizer (`_split_www_authenticate_segments` + `_extract_bearer_auth_params`) explicitly walks segments to find the one whose scheme token matches 'bearer' before collecting its params, so it correctly isolates the Bearer challenge when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. `Bearer ..., Basic ...`). PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only strips text before the first space and treats everything after as one challenge's params, so it does not distinguish a second scheme's params from the first challenge's params in a multi-challenge header. Both diffs are similarly sized single-file changes touching the same function, but #3041's segment-then-scheme-match design covers a case #3012's single-split design does not.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the identical `write_stream, write_stream_reader = create_context_streams[SessionMessage](0)` line to relieve the same zero-capacity stream, but they take different approaches. #2654 changes the default to a buffer of 1 so the fix applies out of the box, and adds a dedicated regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the exact deadlock scenario of queuing a response while a progress notification write is still in flight. #2215 instead adds new `read_stream_buffer_size`/`write_stream_buffer_size` parameters defaulting to 0, so the reported blocking behavior is unchanged unless a caller explicitly opts in by passing a nonzero size — it does not fix the default-path deadlock. #2215 also has a larger API surface (two new public constructor parameters, plus read-stream buffering that is unrelated to the reported issue), while #2654's diff is a minimal, targeted default change with a comment explaining the rationale.

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the exact same branch of validate_tool_use_result_messages() to handle the case where a previous assistant tool_use is not followed by any tool_result block in the next message. The current code unconditionally computes tool_use_ids vs tool_result_ids and raises a generic 'ids do not match' error in this case. #2962 and #3053 propose opposite fixes for this same code path: #2962 skips the id-matching check entirely (via `has_tool_results and ...`) so no error is raised, citing SEP-1577 which states a tool_use is NOT required to be followed by a tool_result. #3053 keeps the original unconditional check's outer guard and instead adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` with a clearer message — i.e. it still treats a missing tool_result as an error, just with better wording. These are mutually exclusive behavioral changes to the same bug, not complementary patches. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041's tokenizer (`_split_www_authenticate_segments` + `_extract_bearer_auth_params`) explicitly walks segments to find the one whose scheme token matches 'bearer' before collecting its params, so it correctly isolates the Bearer challenge when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. `Bearer ..., Basic ...`). PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only strips text before the first space and treats everything after as one challenge's params, so it does not distinguish a second scheme's params from the first challenge's params in a multi-challenge header. Both diffs are similarly sized single-file changes touching the same function, but #3041's segment-then-scheme-match design covers a case #3012's single-split design does not.
